contract_plain_english: For the one-dimensional constant-coefficient scalar specialization of the real linear system, q is real-valued and the constant coefficient is real, making the scalar problem hyperbolic. In the contaminant-transport example, q represents concentration or density and ū is the constant fluid velocity. The asserted equation is ∂_t q(x,t) + ū ∂_x q(x,t) = 0 (raw PDF page 23, equation (1.1), scalar specialization paragraph, and equation (1.2)). The selected passage specifies no initial or boundary data and no explicit regularity class. Its later translated-profile formula is surrounding context, while the derivation is referred to Chapter 2 (same page, text following equation (1.2) and equation (1.3)).
